nahhas-meani:63-63.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوۤاْ أَنَّهُ مَن يُحَادِدِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ﴾.
Its meaning is: he shows enmity and keeps apart. It is said: «حادَّ فلانٌ», that is, he came to be on a side (ḥadd) other than his side.

nahhas-meani:64-64.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَحْذَرُ ٱلْمُنَافِقُونَ أَن تُنَزَّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُورَةٌ تُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِمَا فِي قُلُوبِهِم﴾.
Mujāhid said: These were a group of the hypocrites who spoke about the Prophet ﷺ and the Muslims, and said: We hope that Allah will not disclose [this] about us.

nahhas-meani:65-65.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَئِن سَأَلْتَهُمْ لَيَقُولُنَّ إِنَّمَا كُنَّا نَخُوضُ وَنَلْعَبُ﴾.
The meaning is: And if you ask them about what they said.
Qatāda said: These were a group of the hypocrites who said during the campaign of Tabūk: Does Muḥammad hope to enter the lands of the Byzantines (al-Rūm) and destroy their fortresses? So Allah informed the Prophet ﷺ of what they had said, and he summoned them and said: Did you say such-and-such? They said: ﴿إِنَّمَا كُنَّا نَخُوضُ وَنَلْعَبُ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: They said: If what Muḥammad says is true, then we are donkeys. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed him of what they had said, and he asked them, and they said: We were only chatting and playing.
He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قُلْ أَبِٱللَّهِ وَآيَاتِهِ وَرَسُولِهِ كُنتُمْ تَسْتَهْزِءُونَ؟ لاَ تَعْتَذِرُواْ قَدْ كَفَرْتُمْ بَعْدَ إِيمَانِكُمْ﴾.
That is: disbelief has become manifest from you after belief had been manifest.

nahhas-meani:67-67.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَقْبِضُونَ أَيْدِيَهُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, they do not open them [in giving] for any right, nor for what is obligatory.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿نَسُواْ ٱللَّهَ فَنَسِيَهُمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, He forgot them as regards good; as for evil, He did not forget them.
The meaning according to the people of language is: they abandoned the command of Allah, so He abandoned them, [withholding] His mercy and His granting of success. It is said: «نَسِيَ الشيءَ» when one abandons the thing.

nahhas-meani:68-68.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا هِيَ حَسْبُهُمْ﴾.
That is: it suffices them, that is, it is in proportion to their deeds. And it is said: «أحْسَبَني الشيءُ», that is, the thing sufficed me.

nahhas-meani:69-69.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱسْتَمْتَعُواْ بِخَلاقِهِمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, with their religion. The meaning according to the people of language is: so they enjoyed their share of this world.

nahhas-meani:70-70.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلْمُؤْتَفِكَاتِ﴾.
Qatāda said: They are the cities of the people of Lot.
The people of language said: They were called «مؤتفكات» because they were overturned (ائتفكت) with them, that is, turned upside down. It is from «الإفك», which is lying, because it is inverted and turned away from the truth.

nahhas-meani:73-73.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ جَاهِدِ ٱلْكُفَّارَ وَٱلْمُنَافِقِينَ وَٱغْلُظْ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: That is, strive against the disbelievers with the sword, and against the hypocrites by carrying out the prescribed punishments (ḥudūd) upon them, and with the tongue.
Qatāda said: That is, strive against the disbelievers by fighting, and against the hypocrites by harshness in speech.

nahhas-meani:74-74.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَحْلِفُونَ بِٱللَّهِ مَا قَالُواْ وَلَقَدْ قَالُواْ كَلِمَةَ ٱلْكُفْرِ وَكَفَرُواْ بَعْدَ إِسْلاَمِهِمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: A man from among the Muslims heard them while they were saying: If what Muḥammad has brought is true, then we are donkeys. So he said to them: We say that what he has brought is true — so are we donkeys? Then the hypocrite resolved to kill him, and that is His saying ﴿وَهَمُّواْ بِمَا لَمْ يَنَالُواْ﴾.
Someone other than Mujāhid said: They resolved to kill the Prophet ﷺ, and Allah informed him of that.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَمَا نَقَمُوۤاْ إِلاَّ أَنْ أَغْنَاهُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾.
That is: they resent nothing [in reality], as al-Nābigha said:
وَلاَ عَيْبَ فِيهِمْ غَيْرَ أنَّ سُيُوفَهُمْ * بِهِنَّ فُلُولٌ مِنْ قِرَاعِ الكَتَائِبِ
(There is no fault in them, except that their swords are notched from striking the battalions.)

nahhas-meani:75-75.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّنْ عَاهَدَ ٱللَّهَ لَئِنْ آتَانَا مِن فَضْلِهِ لَنَصَّدَّقَنَّ﴾.
Qatāda said: This was a man of the Anṣār who said: If Allah provides me with something, I shall surely pay its due and I shall surely give charity. But when Allah gave him that, he did what has been related to you. So beware of lying, for it leads to wickedness.
ʿAlī ibn Yazīd narrated from al-Qāsim, from Abū Umāma al-Bāhilī, that Thaʿlaba ibn Ḥāṭib al-Anṣārī came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah to provide me with wealth. He said: Woe to you, O Thaʿlaba! A little for which you give thanks is better than much that you cannot bear. He said: Then he came back to him and said: O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah to provide me with wealth.
He said: Woe to you, O Thaʿlaba! Are you not content to be like the Messenger of Allah? By Allah, if I asked Allah to make the mountains flow for me with gold and silver, they would flow.
Then he came back and said: O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah to provide me with wealth, for by Allah, if Allah gives me wealth I shall surely give everyone who has a right his right. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Allah, provide Thaʿlaba with wealth; O Allah, provide Thaʿlaba with wealth." So he acquired sheep, and they multiplied until the alleys of Medina became too narrow for them, so he moved away with them, and he used to attend the prayers with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then they multiplied until the pastures of
Medina became insufficient for them, so he moved away with them to a place from which he attended the Friday prayers with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then they multiplied and he went far away with them, and he abandoned the Friday prayers and the congregational prayers. Then Allah revealed to His Messenger ﴿خُذْ مِنْ أمْوَالِهِمْ صَدَقةً تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهمْ بِهَا﴾, and the alms-collectors of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out, but he refused them and said: Not until I meet the Messenger of Allah. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّنْ عَاهَدَ ٱللَّهَ لَئِنْ آتَانَا مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾ to the end of the verse — the story. Thaʿlaba was informed, and he came with dust placed on his head until he came to the Prophet ﷺ, but he did not accept [it] from him. Then he came to Abū Bakr, and he did not accept [it] from him. Then he came to ʿUmar, and he refused
to accept [it] from him. Then he came to ʿUthmān, and he did not accept [it] from him, and he died during his caliphate.

nahhas-meani:77-77.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَأَعْقَبَهُمْ نِفَاقاً فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: so Allah caused hypocrisy to follow in them.
And it is possible that the meaning is: so the miserliness caused [hypocrisy] to follow in them, because His saying ﴿بَخِلُوا﴾ indicates miserliness.

nahhas-meani:79-79.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَلْمِزُونَ ٱلْمُطَّوِّعِينَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فِي الصَّدَقَاتِ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, they find fault with the believers. He said: That was because "ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf" gave half of his wealth in charity; his wealth was eight thousand dinars, and he gave four thousand of it in charity. So some people said: How great is his showing-off!
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَلْمِزُونَ ٱلْمُطَّوِّعِينَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فِي الصَّدَقَاتِ﴾. And a man of the Anṣār came with half a heap of dates, and they said: How free of need Allah is of this! So Allah revealed ﴿وَالَّذِينَ لاَ يَجِدُونَ إِلاَّ جُهْدَهُمْ﴾.
[It has been read ﴿جُهْدَهُمْ﴾ and ﴿جَهْدَهُمْ﴾, with ḍamma and with fatḥa.]
Abū Jaʿfar said: They are two dialectal forms with one meaning according to the Basrans.
Some of the Kufans said: «الجَهْد» is hardship, and «الجُهْد» is capacity.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَيَسْخَرُونَ مِنْهُمْ سَخِرَ ٱللَّهُ مِنْهُمْ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾.
The meaning of ﴿سَخِرَ ٱللَّهُ مِنْهُمْ﴾ is: Allah requited them for their mockery; the second was named with the name of the first by way of pairing (al-izdiwāj).

nahhas-meani:80-80.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿#١٦٤٩؛سْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ أَوْ لاَ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ إِن تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً فَلَن يَغْفِرَ ٱللَّهُ لَهُمْ﴾. «[Translator's note: the source text has a corrupted code «#١٦٤٩؛» in place of the opening letters of ٱسْتَغْفِرْ.]»
It is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: I shall surely seek forgiveness for them more than seventy times. Then there was revealed ﴿سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أسْتَغْفَرْتَ لَهُمْ أمْ لَمْ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ﴾, so he abandoned seeking forgiveness for them.

nahhas-meani:81-81.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَرِحَ ٱلْمُخَلَّفُونَ بِمَقْعَدِهِمْ خِلاَفَ رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ وَكَرِهُوۤاْ أَن يُجَاهِدُواْ بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
«الخِلاف» means «المخالفة» (opposition), and the meaning is: for the sake of opposing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, just as you say: «جئتك ابتغاءَ العلمِ» (I came to you seeking knowledge) [Translator's note: i.e. a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose)].
And whoever read ﴿خَلْفَ رَسُولِ اللهِ﴾ meant staying behind from the jihad.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ نَارُ جَهَنَّمَ أشَدُّ حَرًّا﴾.
In it is the meaning of warning and threat.

nahhas-meani:82-82.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَلْيَضْحَكُواْ قَلِيلاً وَلْيَبْكُواْ كَثِيراً جَزَآءً بِمَا كَانُواْ يَكْسِبُونَ﴾.
Abū Razīn said: Allah says: the affair of this world is little, so let them laugh in it as much as they wish, for they will weep in the Fire with a weeping that does not cease — and that is the "much".
Al-Ḥasan said: Let them laugh a little in this world and weep much in the Hereafter, in Hell, as a recompense for what they used to earn.

nahhas-meani:83-83.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱقْعُدُواْ مَعَ ٱلْخَالِفِينَ﴾.
«الخالف» is the one who stays behind with a man's property and in his house.

nahhas-meani:84-84.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ تُصَلِّ عَلَىٰ أَحَدٍ مِّنْهُم مَّاتَ أَبَداً﴾.
It is narrated from Anas ibn Mālik that the Prophet ﷺ stepped forward to pray over "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy", and Gabriel took hold of his cloak and said: ﴿وَلاَ تُصَلِّ عَلَى أَحَدٍ منهم ماتَ أبداً، ولا تَقُمْ عَلَى قَيْرِهِ﴾. «[Translator's note: the source has «قَيْرِهِ», evidently a misprint for «قَبْرِهِ» (his grave).]»
And it is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ, when he prayed over one of them, would stand at his grave and supplicate for him.

nahhas-meani:87-87.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿رَضُواْ بِأَن يَكُونُواْ مَعَ ٱلْخَوَالِفِ وَطُبِعَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ فَهُمْ لاَ يَفْقَهُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: «الخوالف» are the women.
Others besides them said: «الخوالف» are the meanest and basest of people; and it is said: «فلانٌ خالفةُ أهلِهِ» when he is beneath them [in worth].
Abū Jaʿfar said: Its origin is from «خَلَفَ اللَّبَنُ يَخْلُفُ خِلْفَةً», when milk turns sour from standing long; and «خَلَفَ فمُ الصائم», when [the smell of] his breath changes.
And from it is «فلانٌ خَلْفُ سُوءٍ» (so-and-so is a bad successor).
As for Qatāda's saying [on] ﴿فَاقْعُدُوا مَعَ الخَالِفِينَ﴾ — that is, with the women — it is not correct, because the feminine is not pluralised in this way; rather the meaning would be: with those who stay behind for corruption, as has preceded.
And it is possible that the meaning is: with the sick among the men and the chronically disabled.

nahhas-meani:90-90.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَآءَ ٱلْمُعَذِّرُونَ مِنَ ٱلأَعْرَابِ لِيُؤْذَنَ لَهُمْ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās read ﴿وَجَآءَ المُعذِرُونَ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: «الْمُعَذِّرُونَ» admits two meanings:
One of them: that the original meaning is «المعتذرون» (those who offer excuses), then the tāʾ was assimilated into the dhāl; and they would be those who have an excuse. Labīd said:
إلَى الحَوْلِ ثُمَّ اسْمُ السَّلاَمِ عَلَيْكُمَا * وَمَنْ يَبْكِ حَوْلاً كَامِلاً فَقَدِ اعْتَذَرْ.
(Until a year has passed; then the name of peace be upon you both — and whoever weeps a full year has [fully] excused himself.)
And one may offer an excuse when there is no excuse.
The other view: that «المُعَذِّرُون» are those who have no excuse, as it is said: «عَذَّرَ فلانٌ» (so-and-so made [false] excuses / fell short).
Abū al-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad] claimed that «المُعَذَّر» is the one who has no excuse.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is not permissible for it to be in the sense of «المُعْتَذِر», because when ambiguity arises, assimilation (idghām) is not permissible. And «المُعْذَرُونَ» are those who have gone to the utmost in [presenting] excuse; and from this is «قَدْ أَعْذَرَ مَنْ أنْذَرْ» (he who warns has left no excuse), that is, the one who came to you beforehand and warned you has gone to the utmost in excuse.
And «المُعِذِّرُونَ» [would be] «المُعْتَذِرُونَ», [with kasra on the ʿayn] for vowel harmony (al-itbāʿ), the kasra being on the original pattern. «[Translator's note: the source prints this word as «المُعَذِّرُونَ», identical to the first; the context (vowel harmony, kasra) indicates a variant vocalisation is meant.]»

nahhas-meani:92-92.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا مَآ أَتَوْكَ لِتَحْمِلَهُمْ قُلْتَ لاَ أَجِدُ مَآ أَحْمِلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ تَوَلَّوْا وَّأَعْيُنُهُمْ تَفِيضُ مِنَ ٱلدَّمْعِ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan and Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: It was revealed concerning "ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughaffal" of Muzayna, who came to the Prophet ﷺ asking him for a mount.

nahhas-meani:97-97.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلأَعْرَابُ أَشَدُّ كُفْراً وَنِفَاقاً﴾.
Qatāda said: Because they are further from knowing the sunnas (established practices).
Someone else said: Because they are coarser and harder, and further from hearing the Revelation.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَأَجْدَرُ أَلاَّ يَعْلَمُواْ حُدُودَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِ﴾.
That is: and more apt to abandon what Allah has revealed to His Messenger.

nahhas-meani:98-98.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلأَعْرَابِ مَن يَتَّخِذُ مَا يُنفِقُ مَغْرَماً﴾.
That is: a penalty and a loss.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَيَتَرَبَّصُ بِكُمُ ٱلدَّوَائِرَ﴾.
«الدوائر»: that is, the misfortunes that time turns round with; and the origin of «الدوائر» is the vicissitudes of time, at one time with good and at another with evil.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ دَآئِرَةُ ٱلسَّوْءِ﴾.
And it is read: «عَلَيْهِمْ دَائِرَةُ السُّوءِ».
«السُّوء» is affliction and what is disliked, and «السَّوْء» is badness; and it is said: «رَجُلُ سَوْءٍ» and «الرَّجُلُ السَّوْءُ» (a bad man, the bad man).

nahhas-meani:99-99.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلأَعْرَابِ مَن يُؤْمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلآخِرِ وَيَتَّخِذُ مَا يُنفِقُ قُرُبَاتٍ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَصَلَوَاتِ ٱلرَّسُولِ﴾.
Ṣalāt here is supplication.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿وَصَلَوَاتِ ٱلرَّسُولِ﴾ — he says: and the Messenger's seeking forgiveness [for them].
Ṣalāt applies to several kinds:
Ṣalāt from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is mercy, good and blessing. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِى يُصَلِّي عَلَيْكُمْ وَمَلاَئِكَتُهُ﴾.
Ṣalāt from the angels is supplication.
And likewise it is from the Prophet ﷺ, as He, Glorified is He, said: ﴿وَصَلِّ عَلَيْهِمْ إنَّ صَلاَتَكَ سَكَنٌ لَهُمْ﴾.
That is: your supplication is a source of steadfastness and reassurance for them, as the poet said:
تَقُولُ بِنْتِي وَقَدْ قَرَّبْتُ مُرْتَحِلاً * يَا رَبِّ جَنِّبْ أبِي الأوْصَابَ والوَجَعَا
عَلَيْكِ مِثْلُ الَّذِي صَلَّيْتِ فاغْتَمِضِي * نَوْماً فَإنَّ لِجَنْبِ المَرْءِ مُضْطَجَعَا
(My daughter says, as I brought my mount near to depart: "O Lord, keep my father away from ailments and pain." — Upon you be the like of what you have prayed; so close your eyes in sleep, for a man's side [one day] has a resting-place.)

nahhas-meani:100-100.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلسَّابِقُونَ ٱلأَوَّلُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَٱلأَنْصَارِ وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُوهُم بِإِحْسَانٍ﴾.
It is narrated from ʿUmar that he read ﴿والأنْصَارُ﴾.
Whoever read it in the genitive took the meaning to be: and from among the Anṣār.
And whoever read it in the nominative meant the Anṣār all of them, and did not make them part of the forerunners.
Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, Ibn Sīrīn and Qatāda said: ﴿وَٱلسَّابِقُونَ﴾ are those who prayed towards both qiblas.
ʿAṭāʾ said: They are the people of Badr.
Al-Shaʿbī said: They are those who gave the Pledge of Riḍwān.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿رَّضِيَ ٱللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُواْ عَنْهُ﴾.
That is: Allah was pleased with their deeds, and they were pleased with His recompense for them.

nahhas-meani:101-101.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِمَّنْ حَوْلَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلأَعْرَابِ مُنَافِقُونَ وَمِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْمَدِينَةِ مَرَدُواْ عَلَى ٱلنِّفَاقِ﴾.
In the speech there is fronting and postponement (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr); the meaning is: ﴿وَمِمَّنْ حَوْلَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلأَعْرَابِ مُنَافِقُونَ﴾ who have persisted in hypocrisy, ﴿وَمِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْمَدِينَةِ﴾, that is, and from the people of Medina [there are] the like of them.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لاَ تَعْلَمُهُمْ نَحْنُ نَعْلَمُهُمْ سَنُعَذِّبُهُم مَّرَّتَيْنِ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda said: The punishment of this world and the punishment of the grave.
Qatāda said: ﴿ثُمَّ يُرَدُّونَ إِلَىٰ عَذَابٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾, that is, the punishment of Hell.
And it was said: "We shall punish them twice" means captivity and killing.
Al-Farrāʾ said: By killing and the punishment of the grave.
Mujāhid said: By hunger and killing.

nahhas-meani:102-102.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَآخَرُونَ ٱعْتَرَفُواْ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ خَلَطُواْ عَمَلاً صَالِحاً وَآخَرَ سَيِّئاً﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: These were a group who stayed behind from the campaign of Tabūk, among them "Abū Lubāba". They regretted it and tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque, and the Prophet ﷺ said: I do not excuse them. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed: ﴿وَآخَرُونَ ٱعْتَرَفُواْ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ خَلَطُواْ عَمَلاً صَالِحاً وَآخَرَ سَيِّئاً عَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾.
And «عَسَى» from Allah is binding (certain). Then they brought their wealth to the Prophet ﷺ, and he refused to accept it, so Allah revealed ﴿خُذْ مِنْ أمْوَالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ بِهَا، وَصَلِّ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾. «[Translator's note: the source has «فأبى أي يقبَلَها», evidently for «فأبى أن يقبلها»; translated accordingly.]»
Ubayy said: ﴿وَصَلِّ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: and seek forgiveness for them.
And it was said: They are the three who were left behind, and the righteous deed which they did was that they joined the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque, and said: We will not approach family or child until Allah reveals our excuse.
﴿وَآخَرَ سَيِّئاً﴾ is their staying behind from the campaign of Tabūk until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned. The first [view] is the correct one.

nahhas-meani:104-104.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوۤاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ يَقْبَلُ ٱلتَّوْبَةَ عَنْ عِبَادِهِ وَيَأْخُذُ ٱلصَّدَقَاتِ﴾.
That is: and He accepts them.
And from this is ﴿خُذِ العَفْوَ وَأْمُرْ بالعُرْفِ﴾.
And from this is the ḥadīth: "Charity falls into the hand of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He", that is, He accepts it.

nahhas-meani:106-106.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَآخَرُونَ مُرْجَوْنَ لأَمْرِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
That is: deferred.
It is said: «أرجأتُ الأمرَ» (I deferred the matter), and «أَرْجَيْتُ» has also been reported.
And «إمَّا» is for one of two things, so that they would be thus in their [own] view.
And it is said that those deferred here are the three who were left behind, whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, mentioned in His saying ﴿وَعَلَى الثَّلاَثَةِ الَّذِينَ خُلِّفُوا﴾.
ʿIkrima read: ﴿الَّذِينَ خَلَفُوا﴾ with fatḥa on the khāʾ and without doubling, and said: that is, they remained behind after the Prophet ﷺ [had set out].
And the meaning of «خُلِّفوا» is: they were left, their repentance not being accepted [at first], as was read to Bakr ibn Sahl, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from al-Layth, from ʿUqayl, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik, from his father Kaʿb ibn Mālik — and he mentioned the ḥadīth, and said in it: What Allah mentioned is not our staying behind from the campaign; it is only His leaving us behind and His deferring our matter [apart] from those who swore to him, offered him excuses and he accepted from them. He said: "Sahl ibn Saʿd", "Kaʿb ibn Mālik", "Hilāl ibn Umayya" and "Murāra ibn al-Rabīʿ al-ʿAmrī". «[Translator's note: four names are listed here for "the three"; the commonly reported three are Kaʿb ibn Mālik, Hilāl ibn Umayya and Murāra ibn al-Rabīʿ. «خَلَف له» is translated as "swore to him" (حلف له) following the known wording of the ḥadīth.]»
Mujāhid said: They are from al-Aws and al-Khazraj.

nahhas-meani:107-107.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مَسْجِداً ضِرَاراً وَكُفْراً﴾.
That is: and among them are those who took a mosque for harm (ḍirār), that is, for causing harm.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَتَفْرِيقاً بَيْنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَإِرْصَاداً لِّمَنْ حَارَبَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ مِن قَبْلُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He is "Abū ʿĀmir", who went out to Syria seeking Caesar's help in fighting the Muslims, and they were lying in wait for him.
Abū Zayd said: It is said «رصدتُه» in good, and «أرصدتُ له» in evil.
Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: Only «أرصدتُ» is said, and its meaning is: I kept watch [from a height].

nahhas-meani:108-108.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَ تَقُمْ فِيهِ أَبَداً لَّمَسْجِدٌ أُسِّسَ عَلَى ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ مِنْ أَوَّلِ يَوْمٍ أَحَقُّ أَن تَقُومَ فِيهِ﴾.
It is narrated that they invited the Prophet ﷺ to pray in it, as he had prayed in the mosque of Qubāʾ.
Sahl ibn Saʿīd and Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī said: Two men disagreed in the time of the Prophet ﷺ about the mosque that was founded upon piety. One of them said: It is the mosque of the Prophet; and the other said: It is the mosque of Qubāʾ. So they came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "It is this mosque of mine."
And in the ḥadīth of Abū Saʿīd: And in that there is much good.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فِيهِ رِجَالٌ يُحِبُّونَ أَن يَتَطَهَّرُواْ وَٱللَّهُ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُطَّهِّرِينَ﴾.
It is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ asked them about their purification, and they said: "We cleanse ourselves with water [after relieving ourselves]. He said: You have done well."
The hāʾ (pronoun) in His saying ﴿أَحَقُّ أَن تَقُومَ فِيهِ﴾ refers back to the mosque of the Prophet ﷺ.
And the hāʾ in His saying ﴿فِيهِ رِجَالٌ يُحِبُّونَ أَن يَتَطَهَّرُواْ﴾ refers back to the mosque of Qubāʾ; and it is possible that it refers back to the mosque of the Prophet ﷺ.

nahhas-meani:109-109.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَفَمَنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيَانَهُ عَلَىٰ تَقْوَىٰ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِضْوَانٍ خَيْرٌ أَم مَّنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيَانَهُ عَلَىٰ شَفَا جُرُفٍ هَارٍ فَٱنْهَارَ بِهِ فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ﴾.
«الشَّفَا» is the edge and the brink.
«الجُرُف» is what the torrent has eroded.
«الهاري» is what is crumbling and falling.

nahhas-meani:110-110.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَ يَزَالُ بُنْيَانُهُمُ ٱلَّذِي بَنَوْاْ رِيبَةً فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, doubt — as though they were punished with this.
Al-Suddī said: That is, a rankling [in the heart].
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إِلاَّ أَن تَقَطَّعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾.
ʿAṭāʾ, Mujāhid and Qatāda said: ﴿إِلاَّ أَن تَقَطَّعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾: unless they die.
Others said: That is, unless they repent with a repentance in which they regret what they did, until they are like one whose heart has been cut to pieces.
ʿIkrima read: «إلَى أنْ» (until), expressing the limit.

nahhas-meani:111-111.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿نَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱشْتَرَىٰ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنفُسَهُمْ وَأَمْوَالَهُمْ بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ ٱلّجَنَّةَ﴾. «[Translator's note: the source's quotation begins «نَّ» for «إِنَّ».]»
This is a figurative representation (tamthīl), as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أوْلَئِكَ الَّذِينَ اشْتَرَوا الضَّلاَلَةَ بالهُدَى﴾.

nahhas-meani:1-2.t:
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about Sūrat Barāʾa, and he said: That is the Exposer (al-Fāḍiḥa); [verses saying] "and among them…", "and among them…" kept being revealed until we feared it would leave no one out.
And Yazīd al-Fārisī said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: I asked ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān — Allah's mercy be upon him — Why did you take al-Anfāl, which is one of the mathānī, and Barāʾa, which is one of the miʾīn (the surahs of about a hundred verses), and put them together, without separating them with «In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate», and place them with the seven long surahs? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained for a time with the surah of a certain number [of verses] — and in some narrations: with verses — being revealed to him, and perhaps I would ask him and he would say: "Attach it in such-and-such a place", and it resembles such-and-such a story. Barāʾa was among the last to be revealed, and it slipped my mind to ask him about it, so it occurred to my heart that it resembled Sūrat al-Anfāl, and I placed it after it, and did not separate them with "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate".
Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Isḥāq said: One of our companions related to me from our companion "Muḥammad ibn Yazīd" that he said: ﴿بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم﴾ was not written at the beginning of Barāʾa because ﴿بسم الله﴾ is an opening of good, while Barāʾa begins with threat and the breaking of covenants; for that reason ﴿بسم الله﴾ was not written at its beginning.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And the meaning of barāʾa is: a disavowal from Allah and His Messenger ﴿إإِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ عَاهَدْتُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ، فَسِيحُواْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ﴾.
That is: it will be said to them: Travel freely in the land, that is, go and come in safety, for four months; then there is no safety for you after them.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: The four months are: twenty [days] of Dhū l-Ḥijja, al-Muḥarram, Ṣafar, Rabīʿ al-Awwal, and ten [days] of Rabīʿ al-Ākhir.
And al-Zuhrī said: They are Shawwāl, Dhū l-Qaʿda, Dhū l-Ḥijja and al-Muḥarram.
Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَٱعْلَمُوۤاْ أَنَّكُمْ غَيْرُ مُعْجِزِي ٱللَّهِ﴾.
That is: even if you have been granted this respite, the Muslims will be given victory over you.

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿فَإِن تَابُواْ وَأَقَامُواْ ٱلصَّلاَةَ وَآتَوُاْ ٱلزَّكَاةَ فَإِخْوَانُكُمْ فِي ٱلدِّينِ﴾.
That is, they are like you; their breaking of the covenant and their disbelief have been forgiven them.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَإِن نَّكَثُوۤاْ أَيْمَانَهُم مِّن بَعْدِ عَهْدِهِمْ﴾.
That is, they broke [them] and attacked your religion; ﴿فَقَاتِلُوۤاْ أَئِمَّةَ ٱلْكُفْرِ﴾, that is, its chiefs.
And it has been said: This makes killing obligatory for whoever attacks Islam, even if he has a covenant, because that breaks his covenant.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ لاَ أَيْمَانَ لَهُمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَنتَهُونَ﴾.
It is narrated from ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir that he said: That is, they have no covenant. And al-Ḥasan read [لا إيمانَ لهم].
Abū Jaʿfar said: His reading bears two meanings:
One of them: they have no Islam, as a negation, as you say: he has no knowledge.
And the other meaning: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) from your saying آمنتُهُ إيماناً (I granted him safety), that is, do not grant them safety, but kill them.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَهُم بَدَءُوكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: They fought the allies of the Messenger of Allah. Then He said: ﴿أَتَخْشَوْنَهُمْ﴾? That is, do you fear the consequences [from] them? ﴿فَٱللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَن تَخْشَوْهُ﴾, that is, that you fear the consequences [from] Him. Then He promised them victory — and that is one of the signs of prophethood — and said: ﴿قَاتِلُوهُمْ يُعَذِّبْهُمُ اللهُ بأَيْدِيكُمْ، وَيُخْزِهِمْ، وَيَنْصُرْكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ، وَيَشْفِ صُدُورَ قَوْمٍ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾; by this He indicated that their rage had become intense.
Mujāhid said: He means Khuzāʿa, the allies of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَيَتُوبُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَآءُ﴾.
And this is cut off from (i.e. a new sentence, independent of) what precedes it.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَن تُتْرَكُواْ﴾.
That is because, when they were commanded to fight, the hypocrisy of the hypocrites became clear.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَلَمَّا يَعْلَمِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ جَاهَدُواْ مِنكُمْ﴾.
He already knew that with knowledge of the Unseen, but recompense falls only upon witnessed knowledge.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَلَمْ يَتَّخِذُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَلاَ رَسُولِهِ وَلاَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَلِيجَةً﴾.
Al-walīja is: an intimate confidant (biṭāna), from وَلَجَ، يَلِجُ، وُلُوجاً, when he entered; so the meaning is: an intimate attachment of affection, apart from Allah and His Messenger.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ أَن يَعْمُرُواْ مَسَاجِدَ الله﴾ [Translator's note: the context shows that the reading meant here is the singular «مَسْجِدَ الله»; the source prints the plural in both places].
Thus Ibn ʿAbbās read it, and it is the choice of Abū ʿAmr; he adduced as proof His saying, the Exalted: ﴿فَلاَ يَقْرَبُوا المَسْجِدَ الحَرَامَ بَعْدَ عَامِهِمْ هَذَا﴾.
And whoever reads ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ أَن يَعْمُرُواْ مَسَاجِدَ الله﴾, his reading bears two meanings:
One of them: that it refers to all mosques.
And the other: that the Sacred Mosque specifically is meant by it; and this is permissible with what are generic nouns, as one says: So-and-so has come to ride horses, even though he rides only one horse.
And the reading "مساجدَ" is more correct, because it bears both meanings; and they have agreed on reading His saying ﴿إنَّما يَعْمُرُ مَسَاجِدَ اللهِ﴾ in the plural.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿أَجَعَلْتُمْ سِقَايَةَ ٱلْحَاجِّ وَعِمَارَةَ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ كَمَنْ آمَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلآخِرِ﴾.
And the meaning is: Have you made the people of the watering of the pilgrims…, as He said: ﴿وَاسْأَلِ القَرْيَةَ﴾ [Translator's note: i.e. with the muḍāf omitted].
And whoever reads ﴿أَجَعَلْتُمْ سُقَاةَ الحَاجِّ وَعَمَرَةَ المَسْجِدِ الحَرَامِ﴾, for him it involves no ellipsis.
Al-Shaʿbī said: It was revealed concerning ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and al-ʿAbbās.
And al-Ḥasan said: It was revealed concerning ʿAlī, al-ʿAbbās, ʿUthmān ibn Ṭalḥa al-Ḥajabī and Shayba.
And Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Allah's mercy be upon him, went out from Medina to Mecca and said to al-ʿAbbās: O uncle, will you not emigrate? Will you not go to the Prophet ﷺ? He said: I maintain the House and keep its custody. So there was revealed ﴿أَجَعَلْتُمْ سِقَايَةَ ٱلْحَاجِّ﴾ to the end of the verse.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿أَعْظَمُ دَرَجَةً عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
That is, than others; that is, higher in rank than those who give the pilgrims water and those who maintain the Sacred Mosque, and [higher in] jihād [Translator's note: so in the source, «والجهاد»]. ﴿هُمُ ٱلْفَائِزُونَ﴾ with the Garden, those saved from the Fire. And al-fāʾiz is the one who has attained what he hoped for.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿يُبَشِّرُهُمْ رَبُّهُم بِرَحْمَةٍ مِّنْهُ وَرِضْوَانٍ﴾.
That is, He informs them in this world, and [it is] for them in the Hereafter.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَأَذَانٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ إِلَى ٱلنَّاسِ يَوْمَ ٱلْحَجِّ ٱلأَكْبَرِ﴾.
Al-adhān is: announcement.
Shuʿba narrated from al-Ḥakam, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār, who said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, went out to the ʿĪd [prayer] riding a mount, and a man met him and said to him — having taken hold of its bridle — What is the day of "the Greater Pilgrimage"? He said: It is this day of yours that you are in; let go of it.
And likewise the ḥadīth is narrated from ʿAlī.
And Shuʿba narrated from Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said: I heard al-Mughīra ibn Shuʿba giving a sermon on the pulpit, saying: The day of "the Greater Pilgrimage" is the Day of Sacrifice.
And Sufyān narrated from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād, who said: "The Greater Pilgrimage is the Day of Sacrifice, and the lesser pilgrimage is the ʿumra."
And ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr said: I asked ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Awfā about the day of the Greater Pilgrimage, and he said: "The day on which blood is shed and hair is shaved."
And Ḥammād ibn Yazīd narrated from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "The day of the Greater Pilgrimage is the Day of Sacrifice"; and Ibn ʿUmar said likewise.
And someone other than Simāk narrated, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: It is the day of ʿArafa.
And Ibn Jurayj narrated, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, who said: It is the day of ʿArafa.
And Mujāhid said likewise.
And Ibn Sīrīn said: The Greater Pilgrimage is the year in which the Prophet ﷺ performed the pilgrimage; the pilgrimage of the [various] religious communities coincided in it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The most fitting of them is the first view, because of the eminence of those who held it.
And what proves its correctness is the ḥadīth of al-Zuhrī, from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Hurayra: "Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, sent me among those who announced on the Day of Sacrifice at Minā that no idolater shall make the pilgrimage after this year."
And also, people may come to ʿArafāt at night. And the saying of the Prophet ﷺ in the Farewell Pilgrimage: Which day is most sacred? They said: The day of the Greater Pilgrimage. He said: "Then your blood, your wealth and your honour are sacred to you, like the sacredness of this day of yours."
So this indicates that it is the Day of Sacrifice, because Minā is part of the Sanctuary (al-Ḥaram) and ʿArafāt is not part of it. And the view of Ibn Sīrīn is a mistake, because the Muslims and the idolaters performed the pilgrimage a year before that, and it was proclaimed among them that no idolater should perform the pilgrimage after that.
And it is possible that the proclamation was at Minā and at ʿArafāt, so both views would be correct.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ عَاهَدتُّم مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَنقُصُوكُمْ شَيْئاً﴾.
And ʿAṭāʾ ibn Sinān read "ثُمَّ لَمْ يَنْقُضُوكُمْ شَيْئاً" (then they did not break [their covenant with] you in anything).
It is said that this is restricted, meaning the "Banū Ḍamra" specifically. Then He said: ﴿فَأَتِمُّوۤاْ إِلَيْهِمْ عَهْدَهُمْ إِلَىٰ مُدَّتِهِمْ﴾, that is, even if it is more than four months.
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وخُذُوهُمْ﴾, that is, take them captive; and a captive is called akhīdh. ﴿وَاحْصُرُوهُمْ﴾, that is, confine them.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَإِنْ أَحَدٌ مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ ٱسْتَجَارَكَ فَأَجِرْهُ حَتَّىٰ يَسْمَعَ كَلاَمَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
That is, [if] he seeks your protection from being killed so that he may hear the speech of Allah, then grant him protection.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿فَمَا ٱسْتَقَامُواْ لَكُمْ فَٱسْتَقِيمُواْ لَهُمْ﴾.
That is, as long as they keep to the covenant and do not break it, fulfil [it] for them.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿كَيْفَ وَإِن يَظْهَرُوا عَلَيْكُمْ﴾.
Its meaning is: How can they have a covenant, when, if they gain the upper hand over you, they would not observe towards you any illan nor dhimma?
Sufyān narrated from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, who said: Al-ill is Allah, Mighty and Glorious.
And Ibn Jurayj narrated from Mujāhid, who said: Al-ill is the covenant.
And Abū ʿUbayda said: Al-ill is the covenant, and al-dhimma is [the sense of] obligation (al-tadhammum).
And Qatāda said: [Al-ill is] the alliance, and al-dhimma is the covenant.
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Al-ill is kinship, and al-dhimma is the covenant.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And this is the best of them. And the origin of this is that one says: أُذُنٌ مِوَلّلَةٌ [Translator's note: so in the source; the known form is «مُؤَلَّلة»], that is, a sharpened (pointed) ear; and al-alla is the short spear. So when the covenant is called ill, its meaning is that it has been made sharp and definite; and when [the word is used] for kinship, its meaning is that each of the two borders on the other and is close to him. And the philologists recited:
لَعَمْرُكَ إنَّ إلَّكَ مِنْ قُرَيشٍ * كَإلِّ السَّقْبِ مِنْ رَأَلِ النَّعَامِ
(By your life, your kinship (ill) with Quraysh is like the kinship of a camel-colt with an ostrich chick.)
As for what is narrated from Abū Mijlaz and Mujāhid, that al-ill is Allah, Mighty and Glorious, it is not known, because the names of Allah, Mighty and Glorious, are known. And that al-dhimma is the covenant is a known view; and from it come "the people of the dhimma", who are simply the people of the covenant; and تذممتُ أن أفعلَ means: I was ashamed [to do], so you became like one who is under a covenant.

nahhas-meani:112-112.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلتَّائِبُونَ ٱلْعَابِدُونَ ٱلْحَامِدُونَ ٱلسَّائِحُونَ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: That is, those who repent from associating partners [with Allah], who worship Allah alone, «السائحون».
It is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "[They are] those who fast", and this is authentically reported from Ibn Masʿūd.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The origin of «السَّيْح» is going about over the face of the earth; from it is said «ماءٌ سَيْحٌ» (flowing water), and from it Sayḥān was named.
And the one who fasts was called «سايح» because he abandons food, drink and marital relations, so he is in the position of the wanderer.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ٱلرَّاكِعُونَ ٱلسَّاجِدونَ﴾.
That is: those who perform the obligatory duties.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ٱلآمِرُونَ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ﴾, that is, [who enjoin] belief in Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
Then He said: ﴿وَٱلنَّاهُونَ عَنِ ٱلْمُنكَرِ﴾, that is, [who forbid] disbelief.
And it is possible that the meaning is: those who enjoin every good and forbid every evil.
﴿وَٱلْحَافِظُونَ لِحُدُودِ ٱللَّهِ﴾: that is, those who act according to the command and prohibition of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

nahhas-meani:113-113.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ أَن يَسْتَغْفِرُواْ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ وَلَوْ كَانُوۤاْ أُوْلِي قُرْبَىٰ﴾.
Abū al-Khalīl narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "I passed by a man of the Muslims who was seeking forgiveness for his father, who had died an idolater. He said: So I forbade him, and he said: Abraham sought forgiveness for his father. So I came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him, and Allah revealed ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ أَن يَسْتَغْفِرُواْ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ وَلَوْ كَانُوۤاْ أُوْلِي قُرْبَىٰ مِن بَعْدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ أَنَّهُمْ أَصْحَابُ ٱلْجَحِيمِ. وَمَا كَانَ اسْتِغْفَارُ إبْرَاهِيمَ لأِبِيهِ إلاّ عَنْ مَوْعِدَةٍ وَعَدَهَا إيَّاه﴾ to the end of the two verses.
In some narrations: So I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he recited: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ أَن يَسْتَغْفِرُواْ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ — the two verses.
Al-Zuhrī narrated from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ came to Abū Ṭālib when death was approaching him, and "Abū Jahl" and "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umayya" were with him. The Prophet ﷺ said: O uncle, say: "There is no god but Allah", a word by which I will bear witness for you before Allah. Abū Jahl and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Umayya said: Will you turn away from the religion of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib? And he refused to say: There is no god but Allah. So the Prophet ﷺ said: By Allah, I shall surely seek forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ أَن يَسْتَغْفِرُواْ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾, and revealed ﴿إنَّكَ لاَ تَهْدِي مَنْ أحْبَبْتَ وَلَكِنَّ اللهَ يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾. «[Translator's note: the name appears first as «عبدالله بن أمية» and then as «عبدالله بن أبي أمية»; both are kept as written.]»
Ibn Masʿūd said: "The Prophet ﷺ spoke privately at his mother's grave and wept, and said: I asked my Lord's permission to seek forgiveness for her, and He did not permit me. And there was revealed ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ أَن يَسْتَغْفِرُواْ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾."
And it was said: The meaning of ﴿إلاَّ عَنْ مَوْعِدَةٍ وَعَدَهَا إيَّاهُ﴾ is that his father promised him that he would embrace Islam, so he sought forgiveness for him.
﴿فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ أنَّهُ عَدُوٌ للهِ﴾ by his persisting in disbelief, ﴿تَبَرَّأ منه﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās said: When it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, by his dying as a disbeliever, he disassociated himself from him.

nahhas-meani:114-114.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ لأَوَّاهٌ حَلِيمٌ﴾.
Abū Ẓabyān narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: «الأوّاه» is the one who has certainty.
Two views are narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, the soundest of them in chain being what Ḥammād narrated from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from Ibn Masʿūd, that he said: It is the one who supplicates much (al-duʿāʾ); and the other is that it is the merciful.
It is narrated from Mujāhid that it is the one of deep understanding (al-faqīh).
Kaʿb said: When he mentioned the Fire he would sigh "āh".
Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are not contradictory, because all of these are among the attributes of Abraham ﷺ; however, the best of them linguistically is "the one who supplicates much", because «التأوُّه» is only a sound. Al-Muthaqqib said:
إذَا مَا قُمْتُ أرْحَلُهَا بلَيْلٍ * تَأَوَّهُ آهَةَ الرَّجُلِ الحَزِينِ
(Whenever I rise to saddle her by night, she moans with the moan of a grieving man.)
And Kaʿb's saying is also good, that is, he used to sigh when he mentioned the Fire.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: [It is] the one who glorifies [Allah] much. And it was said: the one who sighs over sins and so does not hasten to disobedience. So he only sought forgiveness for his father because of his promise, since seeking forgiveness for a disbeliever is abandoning contentment with the acts of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and His judgements.

nahhas-meani:115-115.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُضِلَّ قَوْماً بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَاهُمْ حَتَّىٰ يُبَيِّنَ لَهُم مَّا يَتَّقُونَ﴾.
Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, may Allah have mercy on him, said: That is, He establishes the proof against them by His command, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَإذَا أرَدْنَا أنْ نُهْلِكَ قَرْيَةً أمَرْنَا مُتْرَفِيهَا فَفَسَقُوا فِيهَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: He makes clear to them the matter of Abraham, that they should not seek forgiveness for the idolaters, specifically; and He makes clear to them obedience and disobedience in general.
And it is narrated that when the prohibition of wine was revealed and made severe, they asked the Prophet ﷺ about those who had died while drinking it. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُضِلَّ قَوْماً بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَاهُمْ حَتَّىٰ يُبَيِّنَ لَهُم مَّا يَتَّقُونَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:117-117.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَقَدْ تَابَ الله عَلَىٰ ٱلنَّبِيِّ وَٱلْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَٱلأَنصَارِ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُوهُ فِي سَاعَةِ ٱلْعُسْرَةِ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl ibn Abī Ṭālib said: "They went out on the campaign of Tabūk in intense heat; two or three men would share a single camel. One day they became extremely thirsty, and they set about slaughtering the camels, splitting open their stomachs and drinking what was in them."
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿مِن بَعْدِ مَا كَادَ يَزِيغُ قُلُوبُ فَرِيقٍ مِّنْهُمْ﴾.
«تَزِيغ»: incline. It was not an inclining away from Islam; they only resolved to turn back, so Allah turned to them in forgiveness and commanded them to it [i.e. to continue].

nahhas-meani:118-118.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَعَلَى ٱلثَّلاَثَةِ ٱلَّذِينَ خُلِّفُواْ حَتَّىٰ إِذَا ضَاقَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلأَرْضُ بِمَا رَحُبَتْ﴾.
Abū Mālik used to say: They were left behind [in the matter of] repentance.
It is reported from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] that the meaning of «خُلِّفُوا» is: they were left, because the meaning of «خلَّفتُ فلاناً» is: you parted from him while he stayed back from what you set out for.
ʿIkrima ibn Khālid read: «خَلَفُوا», that is, they remained after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [had left].
It is narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad that he read «خَالَفُوا» (they opposed).
The meaning of ﴿رَحُبَتْ﴾ is: was spacious.
The meaning of ﴿وَظَنُّوۤاْ أَن لاَّ مَلْجَأَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ إِلاَّ إِلَيْهِ﴾ is: and they were certain.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ تَابَ عَلَيْهِمْ لِيَتُوبُوۤاْ﴾.
There are two answers concerning it:
One of them: that the meaning is: then He turned to them so that they would remain firm in repentance, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا﴾.
The other: that He gave them respite and did not hasten their punishment as He did with others. He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فِبِظُلْمٍ مِنَ الَّذِينَ هَادُوا حَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ طَيِّبَاتٍ أُحِلَّتْ لَهُمْ﴾.

nahhas-meani:119-119.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَـۤأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَكُونُواْ مَعَ ٱلصَّادِقِينَ﴾.
It was said: «مَعَ الصَّادِقِينَ»: those who are truthful in their speech and their deeds.
And it was said: those who are truthful in their faith and fulfil what they have pledged, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ رِجَالٌ صَدَقُوا مَا عَاهَدُوا الله عَلَيْهِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:120-120.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَا كَانَ لأَهْلِ ٱلْمَدِينَةِ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلأَعْرَابِ أَن يَتَخَلَّفُواْ عَن رَّسُولِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
And He said after this: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ المُؤْمِنُونَ لِيَنْفِرُوا كَافَّةً، فَلَوْلاَ نَفَرَ مِنْ كُلِّ فِرْقَةٍ مِنْهُمْ طَائِفَةٌ لِيَتَفَقَّهُوا فِي الدِّينِ﴾.
Qatāda said: They were commanded not to stay behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he went out in person; but when he dispatched an expedition, some of them would stay behind in order to hear the Revelation, the commands and the prohibitions, and inform those who had been absent of it.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning ﴿وَمَا كَانَ المُؤْمِنُونَ لِيَنْفِرُوا كَافَّةً﴾ that it is not about jihad; rather, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invoked years [of drought] against Muḍar, their lands became barren, and a tribe would come in its entirety until they settled in Medina because of hardship, and they wore them [the people of Medina] out. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed [this], informing His Messenger ﷺ that they were not believers. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent them back to their clans and warned their people against doing what they had done. That is His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿وَلِيُنْذِرُوا قَوْمَهُمْ إذَا رَجَعُوا إلَيْهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَحْذَرُونَ﴾.
And with this chain he said: It means the believers should not go out all together and leave the Prophet ﷺ alone. The two interpretations are close to each other, and the meaning is: they do not all go out and leave the guarding of their cities and their upkeep and keeping the enemies away from them; and the guarding of their Prophet ﷺ is incumbent upon them, just as the guarding of their cities from the enemies was lightened for them.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ذٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ لاَ يُصِيبُهُمْ ظَمَأٌ وَلاَ نَصَبٌ وَلاَ مَخْمَصَةٌ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
﴿ظَمَأ﴾: that is, thirst; ﴿وَلاَ نَصَبٌ﴾: and it is the most severe fatigue.
Qatāda said: «المخمصة» is famine.

nahhas-meani:124-124.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا مَآ أُنزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ فَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَقُولُ أَيُّكُمْ زَادَتْهُ هَـٰذِهِ إِيمَاناً﴾.
That is: among the hypocrites is he who says: Which of you has this increased in faith? — because when one believes in it, his faith has increased.

nahhas-meani:125-125.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ﴾.
That is: doubt. ﴿فَزَادَتْهُمْ رِجْساً إِلَىٰ رِجْسِهِمْ﴾: that is, disbelief added to their disbelief.

nahhas-meani:126-126.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوَلاَ يَرَوْنَ أَنَّهُمْ يُفْتَنُونَ فِي كُلِّ عَامٍ مَّرَّةً أَوْ مَرَّتَيْنِ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: That is, they are tested with military campaigns every year, once or twice.
Mujāhid said: That is, they are tested with years of drought and barrenness.

nahhas-meani:127-127.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا مَآ أُنزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ نَّظَرَ بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍ هَلْ يَرَاكُمْ مِّنْ أَحَدٍ﴾.
Because they are hypocrites; so some of them would gesture to others and say: Which of you has this increased in faith? ﴿ثُمَّ ٱنصَرَفُواْ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: then they departed from their place.
And it is possible that the meaning is: then they turned away from faith.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿صَرَفَ ٱللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُم بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لاَّ يَفْقَهُونَ﴾.
Al-Zajjāj said: That is, He led them astray as a requital for their deed.

nahhas-meani:128-128.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَقَدْ جَآءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ﴾.
Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad narrated from his father that he said: There was nothing blameworthy in the lineage of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He ﷺ said: "I am from marriage, not from fornication."
The people of language said: It is possible that the meaning of ﴿لَقَدْ جَآءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ﴾ is: a human being just as you are human beings, so you understand from him.
And it is possible that the meaning is: that he is from the Arabs, so he is from you, and you can ascertain his truthfulness and his way.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿عَزِيزٌ عَلَيْهِ مَا عَنِتُّمْ﴾.
That is: your hardship is grievous to him.
The origin of «العَنَت» is destruction; then what leads to destruction was called «عَنَت».
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿حَرِيصٌ عَلَيْكُمْ بِٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ رَءُوفٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, eager that whoever has not embraced Islam should embrace it.

nahhas-meani:129-129.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَإِن تَوَلَّوْاْ فَقُلْ حَسْبِيَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
That is: Allah suffices me.
It is said: «أحْسبني الشيءُ» when it has sufficed me.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لاۤ إِلَـٰهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَهُوَ رَبُّ ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ﴾.
And the reading of Ibn Muḥayṣin is ﴿وَهُوَ رَبُّ ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ﴾. «[Translator's note: the source prints this reading identically to the standard one; Ibn Muḥayṣin's known reading is «العظيمُ» in the nominative, as an adjective of «ربّ».]»
And it is a good, clear reading.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that the last verse revealed was ﴿لَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾. «[Translator's note: the source has the misprint «ورُوري» for «ورُوي».]»

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿لَقَدْ نَصَرَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِي مَوَاطِنَ كَثِيرَةٍ﴾.
That is, in places; and from it comes: استوطَنَ فلان المكان, that is, he settled in the place.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَيَوْمَ حُنَيْنٍ إِذْ أَعْجَبَتْكُمْ كَثْرَتُكُمْ﴾.
That is, and He helped you on the day of Ḥunayn.
Qatāda said: Ḥunayn is the name of a watering place between Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif. He said: "The Prophet ﷺ was with twelve thousand of the Emigrants and the Anṣār, and two thousand of the ṭulaqāʾ (those freed at the Conquest of Mecca). A man said: You will not be defeated today. Then most of them scattered." Then the Prophet ﷺ supplicated, and he was answered and given victory. So Allah, Mighty and Glorious, let them know that they do not prevail through great numbers, but only prevail by Allah's giving them victory.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ إِنَّمَا ٱلْمُشْرِكُونَ نَجَسٌ﴾.
Everything considered filthy is called najas; and when you say rijs, nijs, you give kasra to the rāʾ and the nūn and put sukūn on the jīm.
* And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿فَلاَ يَقْرَبُواْ ٱلْمَسْجِدَ ٱلْحَرَامَ بَعْدَ عَامِهِمْ هَـٰذَا﴾.
Ibn Jurayj narrated from ʿAṭāʾ, who said: By the Sacred Mosque He means the entire Sanctuary (al-ḥaram).
And Ibn Jurayj narrated, from Abū l-Zubayr, from Jābir: ﴿إِنَّمَا ٱلْمُشْرِكُونَ نَجَسٌ فَلاَ يَقْرَبُواْ ٱلْمَسْجِدَ ٱلْحَرَامَ﴾ — except if he is a slave or one of the people of the jizya (poll-tax).
And this is the position of the Kufans: that by "the idolaters" in the verse are meant those who have no covenant [and that this applies to all mosques] [Translator's note: so in the source].
And the position of the Medinans is that the verse is general to all unbelievers, and that they are to be kept away from all mosques.
And the position of al-Shāfiʿī is that "the idolaters" here is likewise general, like the view of Mālik, except that he said: That applies only to the Sacred Mosque specifically.
And the position of the Medinans on this is the best, because of the saying of Allah, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿فِي بُيُوتٍ أَذِنَ اللهُ أن تُرْفَعَ﴾, that is, be protected; so according to this it is obligatory that they be kept elevated above their entering, because they do not honour them when they enter.
* And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ عَيْلَةً﴾.
And al-ʿayla is poverty; one says: عَالَ، يَعِيلُ، عَيْلَةً; and from it comes ﴿وَوَجَدَكَ عَائِلاً فَأَغْنَى﴾.
And ʿAlqama said: In the codex of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd [it is] ﴿وإنْ خِفْتُمْ عَائِلةً﴾, and its meaning is: a burdensome circumstance; one says: عالني الأمر يَعْولني, that is, it was burdensome and hard on me.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿قَاتِلُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَلاَ بِٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلآخِرِ﴾.
The meaning is: Fight those who do not believe in Allah with the faith of those who affirm His oneness; because the People of the Book believe in Allah and say: He has a son — exalted is He above that.
And they believe in the Hereafter and say: There is no eating in it and no drinking; and this is contrary to what Allah, Mighty and Glorious, has commanded for it.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَلاَ يَدِينُونَ دِينَ ٱلْحَقِّ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: Its sense (majāz) is: and they do not obey with the obedience of the truth.
Abū Jaʿfar said: That is, the obedience of the people of Islam. And everyone who obeys a king is dāʾin to him; one says: دَانَ فلانٌ لفلانٍ (so-and-so submitted to so-and-so).
Zuhayr said:
لَئِنْ حَلَلْتَ بِجَوٍّ فِي بَنِي أَسَدٍ * فِي دِينِ عَمْروٍ، وَحَالَتْ دُونَنَا فَدَكُ
(If you settle in Jaww among the Banū Asad, under the sway (dīn) of ʿAmr, and Fadak stands between us…)
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ﴾.
They are the Jews and the Christians; and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ established as a practice that the Magians be treated as they are.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿حَتَّىٰ يُعْطُواْ ٱلْجِزْيَةَ عَن يَدٍ وَهُمْ صَاغِرُونَ﴾.
Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying, Mighty and Glorious, ﴿وَهُمْ صَاغِرُونَ﴾: He said: They walk with it, being led by the collar (mulabbabīn) [Translator's note: the source has «مُلَبِّينَ»].
And ʿAṭāʾ narrated from Abū l-Bakhtarī, from Salmān, who said: Blameworthy.
And Muḥammad ibn Thawr narrated, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda: ﴿عَن يَدٍ﴾ — he said: from a dower (mahr) [Translator's note: so in the source, «عن مَهْرٍ»; perhaps a corruption of «عن قهر», "under compulsion"].
And it has been said: The meaning of (يَدٍ) is "from the bestowal of a hand [of favour]", that is, from a favour from you to them, because when the jizya is taken from them, they have been favoured thereby.
And it has been said — and it is the soundest of them —: they pay it with their own hands and do not send it [by others], as tyrants do.
And Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: He hands it over while standing, and the one who takes it from him is seated.
And most of the philologists hold that the meaning is: under compulsion and abasement, as you say: The upper hand (al-yad) in this belongs to so-and-so.
And the position of al-Shāfiʿī on this is that the jizya is taken from them while the rulings of the Muslims are applied to them.
Then He said: ﴿وَهُمْ صَاغِرُونَ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: Al-ṣāghir is the abased, the despised.
And someone else said: The one who is shaken about and treated roughly.

nahhas-meani:30-30.t:
Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿ذٰلِكَ قَوْلُهُم بِأَفْوَاهِهِمْ﴾.
It may be said: It is known that speech is with the mouth, so what is the benefit of His saying ﴿بِأَفْوَاهِهِمْ﴾?
And the answer to this is that they have no clear exposition and no proof, because they say: Allah has taken a consort, and they say: He has a son; and their saying is without any argument.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿يُضَاهُونَ قَوْلَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن قَبْلُ﴾.
That is, they resemble and follow in the footsteps of what they said.
And it is read ﴿يُضَاهِئونَ﴾, and the meaning is the same. One says: امرأةٌ ضَهْيَا, with short final alif, and ضَهْيَاءُ, with long final alif and diptote, when she does not menstruate.
And it is said: She is the one who has no breasts.
And the meaning is that she has resembled men in this trait. So whoever takes the hamza to be radical says ﴿يُضَاهِئُونَ﴾, and whoever takes it to be augmentative — and that is better — says ﴿يُضَاهُونَ﴾.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿قَاتَلَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّىٰ يُؤْفَكُونَ﴾.
So they were addressed with what they know, that is, it is fitting that this be said to them.
Then He said: ﴿أَنَّىٰ يُؤْفَكُونَ﴾? That is, from where are they turned away from the truth after the clear exposition?

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿ٱتَّخَذُوۤاْ أَحْبَارَهُمْ وَرُهْبَانَهُمْ أَرْبَاباً مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash and Sufyān narrated from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Abū l-Bakhtarī, who said: Ḥudhayfa was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Glorious, ﴿ٱتَّخَذُوۤاْ أَحْبَارَهُمْ وَرُهْبَانَهُمْ أَرْبَاباً مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ﴾: Did they worship them? He said: No, but they made the unlawful lawful for them and they treated it as lawful, and they made the lawful unlawful for them and they treated it as unlawful.
Abū Jaʿfar related to us, saying: Abū l-Qāsim "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad, the son of the daughter of Aḥmad ibn Manīʿ" related to us, saying: al-Ḥimmānī related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Salām ibn Ḥarb related to us, from Ghuḍayf — he is Ibn Aʿyan — from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, from ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim, who said: The Prophet ﷺ saw a cross of gold on my neck and said: Throw this off you. He said: And he was asked about His saying, the Exalted, ﴿ٱتَّخَذُوۤاْ أَحْبَارَهُمْ وَرُهْبَانَهُمْ أَرْبَاباً مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ﴾? He said: As for them, they did not worship them, but they would make lawful for them what Allah had made unlawful for them, and they would treat it as lawful; and they would make unlawful for them what Allah had made lawful for them, and they would treat it as unlawful.

nahhas-meani:34-34.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يَكْنِزُونَ ٱلذَّهَبَ وَٱلْفِضَّةَ وَلاَ يُنفِقُونَهَا فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: and they do not spend the treasures, because the treasures here comprise gold and silver.
And it is possible that it [the pronoun] refers to one of the two, as He said: ﴿واللهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أحَقُّ أن يُرْضُوهُ﴾.
And there are several views on this verse:
ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, and ʿAṭiyya and Nāfiʿ from Ibn ʿUmar, that they both said: "Whatever has had its zakāt paid is not a hoard (kanz)."
And what strengthens that is that Ibn Jurayj narrated from Abū l-Zubayr, from Jābir, from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "When you have paid the zakāt of your wealth, you have removed its evil from yourself."
And it has been said that this verse was revealed concerning the idolaters.
And Abū Hurayra said: "Whoever leaves behind ten thousand, it will be made into plates and he will be punished with them until the reckoning is over."
And Abū Umāma said: "Whoever leaves behind white or yellow [silver or gold] will be branded with it, whether forgiven or not forgiven; and the ornamentation of a sword is part of that."
And Mūsā ibn ʿUbayda narrated, from ʿImrān ibn Abī Anas, from Mālik ibn Aws ibn al-Ḥadathān, from Abū Dharr, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever gathers a dinar or a dirham, or gold dust, or silver, not setting it aside for a creditor nor spending it in the way of Allah, it is a hoard with which he will be branded on the Day of Resurrection."
And Muʿāwiya said: It was revealed concerning the People of the Book; but Abū Dharr rejected that and said: It was revealed concerning us and them.
And the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar on this is good, considering his caution, and it has a good chain: Mālik, Ayyūb and ʿUbaydallāh narrated it, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar.
And it has also been narrated from ʿUmar that he said: "What you have paid the zakāt of is not a hoard."
And Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab and ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said likewise, except that he said: I consider it abrogated, by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً تُطَهِّرْهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ بِهَا﴾; but in a report (khabar) there is neither abrogating nor abrogated.
And Abū l-Zubayr narrated from Jābir, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "There is no servant who does not pay the zakāt of his wealth but that his wealth will be brought to him and heated for him in the fire of Hell, and his sides, his forehead and his back will be branded with it, until Allah judges between His servants…" And he mentioned the ḥadīth.

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿إِنَّ عِدَّةَ ٱلشُّهُورِ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ ٱثْنَا عَشَرَ شَهْراً فِي كِتَابِ ٱللَّهِ يَوْمَ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ مِنْهَآ أَرْبَعَةٌ حُرُمٌ﴾.
The four sacred [months] are: "al-Muḥarram, Rajab, Dhū l-Qaʿda and Dhū l-Ḥijja".
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿ذٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْقَيِّمُ﴾.
Al-dīn here is: the reckoning; that is, that is the correct reckoning and the complete count.
And from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿ذٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْقَيِّمُ﴾ — he said: the upright decree.
And Abū ʿUbayda said: That is, the standing (al-qāʾim).
﴿فَلاَ تَظْلِمُواْ فِيهِنَّ أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾.
Most of the exegetes hold that the meaning is: do not wrong yourselves in the four; and He singled them out to magnify them, as He said: ﴿فَلاَ رَفَثَ وَلاَ فُسُوقَ وَلاَ جِدَالَ فِى الحَجِّ﴾.
And Ḥammād ibn Salama narrated from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿فَلاَ تَظْلِمُواْ فِيهِنَّ أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ — in the twelve.
And Qays ibn Muslim narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya, who said: In all of them.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿إِنَّمَا ٱلنَّسِيۤءُ زِيَادَةٌ فِي ٱلْكُفْرِ﴾.
Al-nasīʾ is: postponement; and from it comes: نَسَأَ اللهُ في أَجَلك (may Allah prolong your term).
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿يُضَلُّ بِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ﴾.
Al-Zuhrī, Qatāda, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Abū Wāʾil and al-Shaʿbī said: They would sometimes postpone the sanctity of al-Muḥarram to Ṣafar.
Qatāda said: And they used to call them: the two Ṣafars.
And Mujāhid said: They had reckoners who did calculations, and they would sometimes say to them: The pilgrimage this year is in al-Muḥarram, and they would accept it from them.
And what indicates this is His saying: ﴿وَلاَ جِدَالَ فى الحَجِّ﴾, that is, it is in Dhū l-Ḥijja.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The clearest thing on this is what Bakr ibn Sahl related to us, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us, from Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿إِنَّمَا ٱلنَّسِيۤءُ زِيَادَةٌ فِي ٱلْكُفْرِ﴾ — he said: Junāda ibn Umayya used to come to the season [of pilgrimage] every year, and he was given the kunya "Abū Thumāma", and he would call out: Lo, Abū Thumāma is not disappointed and is not faulted! Lo, the Ṣafar of the first year is this year lawful [Translator's note: the wording «ألاَ وإن صفر العامِ الأولِ العامَ حلالٌ» is so in the source]. So he would make it lawful for the people; and he would make Ṣafar sacred one year and make al-Muḥarram sacred another year. That is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿إِنَّمَا ٱلنَّسِيۤءُ زِيَادَةٌ فِي ٱلْكُفْرِ﴾, the verse. He said: And al-nasīʾ is their leaving al-Muḥarram [unsacred] one year, and another year making it sacred.
And al-Ḥasan read ﴿يُضِلُّ بِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ﴾ [with the active], meaning by "those who disbelieved" the reckoners who told them this.
And it is narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: ﴿يُضِلُّ بِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ﴾, that is, those who accept it from the reckoners are led astray by it [Translator's note: so in the source; the gloss fits the passive reading يُضَلُّ].
And an argument for those who hold the first view is His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿يُحِلُّونَهُ عَاماً وَيُحَرِّمُونَهُ عَاماً لِّيُوَاطِئُواْ عِدَّةَ مَا حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ﴾, that is, to match, so that they make four [months] sacred just as Allah, Mighty and Glorious, made four sacred.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ مَا لَكُمْ إِذَا قِيلَ لَكُمُ ٱنفِرُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ٱثَّاقَلْتُمْ إِلَى ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: In the expedition [Translator's note: the source has the misprint «عزوة» for «غزوة»] of Tabūk; they were commanded to go out in intense heat when the fruits had ripened, and they said: To the shade!
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿أَرَضِيتُمْ بِٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا مِنَ ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾.
That is, are you content with the comforts of the life of this world in place of the comforts of the Hereafter!
﴿فَمَا مَتَاعُ ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا فِي ٱلآخِرَةِ إِلاَّ قَلِيلٌ﴾.
And al-matāʿ is: benefit and comfort.

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿إِلاَّ تَنصُرُوهُ فَقَدْ نَصَرَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِذْ أَخْرَجَهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ثَانِيَ ٱثْنَيْنِ إِذْ هُمَا فِي ٱلْغَارِ﴾.
Al-Zuhrī said: He and Abū Bakr went out and entered a cave in Mount Thawr, and stayed in it three [nights].
And the meaning is: Allah helped him as the second of two, that is, Allah helped him when he was alone, except for Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him.
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿فَأَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلَيْهِ﴾.
It is possible that it [the pronoun] refers to "Abū Bakr" [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense suggests the first possibility should be the Prophet ﷺ], and the more likely — according to the view of the people of speculative reasoning — is that it refers to Abū Bakr, because the Prophet ﷺ already had tranquillity (al-sakīna) upon him — and it is calm and reassurance — since He, Mighty and Glorious, reported of him that he said: ﴿لاَ تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَنَا﴾. And I shall mention this in the I'rab [book] with the fullest explanation.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿ٱنْفِرُواْ خِفَافاً وَثِقَالاً﴾.
There are several views on the meaning of this, among them:
That Anas ibn Mālik narrated that "Abū Ṭalḥa" interpreted it as: young and old.
And al-Miqdād said: I find myself only either lightly or heavily burdened [Translator's note: the source has «ألا» for «إلا»].
And al-Ḥasan said: In hardship and ease.
And Sufyān narrated from Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Malak al-Ghifārī, who said: The first [part] of Sūrat Barāʾa to be revealed was ﴿ٱنْفِرُواْ خِفَافاً وَثِقَالاً﴾.
And Abū l-Ḍuḥā said likewise.
Then its beginning and its end were revealed.
And Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿ٱنْفِرُواْ خِفَافاً وَثِقَالاً﴾ — he said: Among them were the heavily burdened, and the one in need, and the one with an estate, and the one with business; and Allah, Mighty and Glorious, sent down ﴿ٱنْفِرُواْ خِفَافاً وَثِقَالاً﴾.
And Sufyān narrated from Manṣūr concerning His saying ﴿ٱنْفِرُواْ خِفَافاً وَثِقَالاً﴾: He said: Busy and not busy.
And Qatāda said — and it is the position of al-Shāfiʿī —: Riding and on foot.
And Qatāda said: Eager and not eager.
And Zayd ibn Aslam said: The heavily burdened is the one who has dependants, and the lightly burdened is the one who has no dependants.
And this was when the people of Islam were few; then there was revealed ﴿ومَا كَانَ المُؤمِنُونَ لِيَنْفِرُوا كَافَّةً﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are close to one another.
And the meaning is: go forth in every circumstance.
And among the most comprehensive of these views is the view of al-Ḥasan.
Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Kinānī related to us in al-Anbār, saying: Naṣr ibn ʿAlī related to us, saying: My father informed me, saying: Shuʿba related to us, from Manṣūr ibn Zādhān, from al-Ḥasan: ﴿ٱنْفِرُواْ خِفَافاً وَثِقَالاً﴾ — he said: In hardship and ease.
And the view of Abū Ṭalḥa is good, because movement is light for the young man and heavy for the old man.

nahhas-meani:42-42.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿لَوْ كَانَ عَرَضاً قَرِيباً وَسَفَراً قَاصِداً لاَّتَّبَعُوكَ﴾.
Al-ʿaraḍ is whatever presents itself of the benefits of this world; that is, had it been near booty and a moderate journey, that is, an easy one, they would have followed you. ﴿وَلَـٰكِن بَعُدَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلشُّقَّةُ﴾ — and al-shuqqa is the destination one heads for.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿عَفَا ٱللَّهُ عَنكَ لِمَ أَذِنتَ لَهُمْ حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكَ ٱلَّذِينَ صَدَقُواْ وَتَعْلَمَ ٱلْكَاذِبِينَ﴾ [43].
That is, until it becomes clear who was hypocritical and who was not.
Mujāhid said: These were people who said: We will ask leave to stay behind; if we are given leave, we stay behind, and if we are not given leave, we stay behind.
And Qatāda said: He abrogated this verse by His saying in Sūrat al-Nūr: ﴿فَإِنْ اسْتَأْذَنُوكَ لِبَعْضِ شَأْنِهِمْ فَأْذَنْ لِمَنْ شِئْتَ مِنْهُمْ﴾.
Then He made clear that the sign of disbelief is asking leave to stay behind, and the Exalted said: ﴿لاَ يَسْتَأْذِنُكَ الَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللهِ واليَوْمِ الآخِرِ أَنْ يُجَاهِدُوا بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾.

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَلَوْ أَرَادُواْ ٱلْخُرُوجَ لأَعَدُّواْ لَهُ عُدَّةً وَلَـٰكِن كَرِهَ ٱللَّهُ ٱنبِعَاثَهُمْ فَثَبَّطَهُمْ﴾.
Al-tathbīṭ is: holding a person back from what he wants to do.

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿لَوْ خَرَجُواْ فِيكُم مَّا زَادُوكُمْ إِلاَّ خَبَالاً﴾.
Al-khabāl is: corruption, and the ruin of a thing.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿ولأَوْضَعُواْ خِلاَلَكُمْ يَبْغُونَكُمُ ٱلْفِتْنَةَ﴾.
Al-īḍāʿ is: speed of travel.
Abū Isḥāq said: The meaning of ﴿خِلاَلَكُمْ﴾ is: in whatever undermines you.
And someone else said: among you.
And it has been said: Al-fitna here is: idolatry (shirk).
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَفِيكُمْ سَمَّاعُونَ لَهُمْ﴾.
There are two views on it:
One of them: among you are those who listen and tell them what they want.
And the other view: among you are those who accept from them, like "سَمِعَ اللهُ لمن حَمِدَه" (Allah accepts [lit. hears] from whoever praises Him).
And the first view is more fitting, because it is the predominant of its two meanings — that the meaning of sammāʿ is one who listens to speech; and like it [Translator's note: the source has the misprint «زمثله» for «ومثله»] is ﴿سَمَّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ﴾.
And [as for] the second view: in it one would hardly say anything but "sāmiʿ", like qāʾil.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَقُولُ ٱئْذَن لِّي وَلاَ تَفْتِنِّي﴾.
There are two views on it:
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: And do not make me a disbeliever; and likewise Qatāda said: That is, and do not make me sinful.
And its meaning is: do not make me sinful by [commanding me to] go out when it is not easy for me, so that if I stay behind I become sinful.
And the other view, which is the view of Mujāhid, is that it was said to them: You will go on campaign and take the daughters of the Yellow ones (Banāt al-Aṣfar, i.e. the Byzantines) as spoils; and one of them said: Do not tempt me with the daughters of the Yellow ones.
Abū Isḥāq said: [It was revealed] concerning "al-Jadd ibn Qays", one of the Banū Salima, and he is the one who said this.

nahhas-meani:50-50.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿إِن تُصِبْكَ حَسَنَةٌ تَسُؤْهُمْ﴾.
That is, if you are victorious and gain spoils, that grieves them; ﴿وَإِن تُصِبْكَ مُصِيبَةٌ﴾ — you are defeated — ﴿يَقُولُواْ قَدْ أَخَذْنَا أَمْرَنَا مِن قَبْلُ﴾, that is, we have taken precautions, since we did not go out likewise.
And Mujāhid said: Its meaning is: we were on our guard.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿قُل لَّن يُصِيبَنَآ إِلاَّ مَا كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ لَنَا﴾.
There are two views on its meaning:
One of them: except what Allah has decreed for us.
And the other: except what He has informed us of in His Book, that we are killed and become martyrs, or that we kill you.
And likewise is the meaning of ﴿قُلْ هَلْ تَرَبَّصُونَ بِنَا إلاَّ إحْدَى الحُسْنَيَيْنِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:55-55.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿فَلاَ تُعْجِبْكَ أَمْوَالُهُمْ وَلاَ أَوْلاَدُهُمْ إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ بِهَا فِي ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾.
It contains fronting and postponement (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr).
The meaning is: Let not their wealth nor their children impress you in the life of this world; Allah only intends to punish them in the Hereafter.
And this is the view of most of the grammarians (ahl al-ʿarabiyya).
And it is possible that the meaning is: Let not their wealth nor their children impress you; Allah only intends to punish them with them in this world, because they are hypocrites, so they spend unwillingly, and are punished by what they spend.
Then He said: ﴿وَتَزْهَقَ أَنفُسُهُمْ﴾, that is, [their souls] depart.

nahhas-meani:57-57.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿لَوْ يَجِدُونَ مَلْجَئاً أَوْ مَغَارَاتٍ أَوْ مُدَّخَلاً لَّوَلَّوْاْ إِلَيْهِ وَهُمْ يَجْمَحُونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: Al-maljaʾ is fortresses; al-maghārāt is caves; and al-muddakhal is tunnels.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And this is a good view according to the philologists, because a fortress is called maljaʾ and lajaʾ; and al-maghārāt is from غَارَ يَغورُ, when it is concealed.
And it is read ﴿أَوْ مُدَّخَلاً﴾ with doubled dāl and khāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; only the dāl is doubled], and it is read ﴿أوْ مُدْخلاً﴾, and it is read ﴿أوْ مَدْخلاً﴾. Their meanings are close, except that "مَدْخلاً" is from دَخَل يَدْخُلُ, and "مُدْخلاً" is from أَدْخَلَ يُدْخِلُ; that is, if they could find a people who would admit them into their number, or a people who would enter with them, or a place they could enter, ﴿لَّوَلَّوْاْ إِلَيْهِ﴾, that is, if they found one of these things, ﴿لَّوَلَّوْاْ إِلَيْهِ وَهُمْ يَجْمَحُونَ﴾, that is, they would rush, with nothing turning their faces back.
And from it comes: فَرَسٌ جموحٌ (a runaway horse).

nahhas-meani:58-58.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَلْمِزُكَ فِي ٱلصَّدَقَاتِ فَإِنْ أُعْطُواْ مِنْهَا رَضُواْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, he tests you and asks you.
And Qatāda said: That is, he attacks you.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And the view according to the philologists is the view of Qatāda; one says: لَمَزَهُ، يَلْمِزُه, when he found fault with him. And from it comes: فلانٌ هُمَزَةٌ لُمَزَةٌ, that is, one who finds fault with people a great deal.
And it is said: The lumaza is the one who finds fault in secret, and the humaza is the one who signals with his eyes.
And all of this goes back to his finding fault.

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿إِنَّمَا ٱلصَّدَقَاتُ لِلْفُقَرَآءِ وَٱلْمَسَاكِينِ﴾.
Qatāda said: The «فقير» is the needy person who has a chronic disability, and the «مسكين» is the healthy needy person.
And Mujāhid and al-Zuhrī said: The «فقير» is the one who does not beg, and the «مسكين» is the one who begs.
Muḥammad ibn Idrīs ibn Aswad related to us, saying: Yūnus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim informed me, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: "The «فقراء» are from the Emigrants, and the «مساكين» are from the Bedouins."
He said: And Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: The «فقراء» are from the Muslims, and the «مساكين» are from the people of the dhimma.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What al-Zuhrī and Mujāhid said is good, because «مسكين» is taken from sukūn (stillness) and submissiveness; and on those who beg, stillness and submissiveness are apparent.
And even if the one who begs and the one who does not beg share the name of poverty, the one who [begs] [Translator's note: the source has «الطي», apparently a misprint for «الذي»] shows, together with poverty, what we have mentioned.
And «فقير» in the language is only understood by saying: [in need] of such-and-such.
So the meaning is: those in need («فقراء») of charity; and a «مسكين» is one on whom there is abasement, because one may be in need of it without there being any abasement on him in it.
And the philologists said — we know of no disagreement among them —:
The «فقير» is the one who has a bare sufficiency (bulgha), and the «مسكين» is the one who has nothing.
And they recited:
أمَّا الفَقِيرُ الَّذي كَانَتْ حَلُوبتُهُ * وَفْقَ العِيَالِ فَلَمْ يُتْرَكْ لَهُ سَبَدُ.
(As for the poor man whose milch-camel was just enough for his household, not a single hair [i.e. nothing at all] was left to him.)
And Yūnus said: I said to a Bedouin: Are you «فقير»? He said: No, rather «مسكين».
And Abū Hurayra narrated from the Prophet ﷺ: "The «مسكين» is not the one who goes around [begging], who is turned away with a morsel or two, and a date or two; rather the «مسكين» is the one who does not beg, and is not noticed so as to be given, and does not find sufficiency to make him independent."
Abū Jaʿfar said: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: «فقير» is derived from their saying فَقَرْتُ له فَقْرَةً من مالي, that is, I gave him a portion; so the «فقير» [on this view] is the one who has a portion of wealth. And «مسكين» is taken from sukūn (stillness), as though he were in the position of one who has no movement.
And some of the jurists said: The «مسكين» is the one who has something; and he adduced as proof the saying of Allah, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿أمَّا السَّفِينَةُ فَكَانتْ لِمَسَاكِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ فِى البَحْرِ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This argument is not binding, because you say: This fruit is for (li-) this palm, and this house is for (li-) this dwelling, not intending ownership; so it is possible that "لمساكين" was said because they worked on it.
And it has been said that it is merely a figure of speech, as the Prophet ﷺ said to one of the women: "O miskīna, be tranquil."
Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَٱلْعَامِلِينَ عَلَيْهَا﴾
They are the collectors and those like them.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَٱلْمُؤَلَّفَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾.
Al-Shaʿbī said: These were people whose hearts were won over in the time of the Prophet ﷺ; when Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, took office, this ceased.
