Abū Jaʿfar said: The report of al-Shaʿbī was narrated from him only by Jābir al-Juʿfī; and Yūnus said: I asked al-Zuhrī, and he said: I do not know that anything of that has been abrogated.
So on this basis the ruling concerning them is established: if there is someone whose heart needs to be won over, and it is feared that some harm will befall the Muslims from him, or it is hoped that his Islam will become good afterwards, [a share] is given to him.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَفِي ٱلرِّقَابِ﴾.
That is, and for freeing necks (slaves).
It has been said: They are the mukātabs (slaves contracted to buy their freedom).
And it has been said: Slaves are bought, and the walāʾ (clientage) belongs to the Muslims.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَٱلْغَارِمِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: "They are those whose houses fire has burned and whose wealth a flood has carried away, so they went into debt for their dependants."
And it is narrated from Abū Jaʿfar, Mujāhid and Qatāda that they said: The ghārim is one who has taken a loan for something other than disobedience.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And it cannot be otherwise, because if he had a debt in disobedience and it was paid off for him, he would have been helped in disobedience.
And al-ghurm in the language is: loss; so it is as though the debtor who cannot find the means to pay his debt has lost his wealth. And from it comes ﴿إنَّ عَذَابَهَا كَانَ غَرَاماً﴾, that is, destruction and loss.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَفِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾, that is, in obedience to Allah, that is, for those fighting in jihād and the pilgrims; ﴿وَٱبْنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ﴾.
Jābir narrated from Abū Jaʿfar that he said: He is the one passing through from land to land.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And al-sabīl in the language is: the road; so ibn al-sabīl is the one who has been waylaid on the road, or has come from enemy territory with his wealth taken.
The jurists said: The wayfarers are those away from their wealth who cannot reach it because of the distance between them and it, so that they come to need charity; so it is then permissible for them, for they have come under the ruling of one who has no wealth.
Al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr narrated, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, from Ḥudhayfa, concerning His saying, the Exalted, ﴿إِنَّمَا ٱلصَّدَقَاتُ لِلْفُقَرَآءِ وَٱلْمَسَاكِينِ﴾.
He said: Allah only mentioned these [categories for] charities so that they would be known; whichever category you give to from them, it suffices you.
And Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿إِنَّمَا ٱلصَّدَقَاتُ لِلْفُقَرَآءِ وَٱلْمَسَاكِينِ﴾ — he said: In whichever of them you place it, it suffices for you.

nahhas-meani:61-61.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَمِنْهُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْذُونَ ٱلنَّبِيَّ وَيِقُولُونَ هُوَ أُذُنٌ﴾.
Mujāhid said: These were some of the hypocrites; they spoke of the Prophet ﷺ and said: Let us say [what we like] about him; if that reaches him, we will swear to him and he will believe us.
And likewise udhun in the language: one says: هو أُذُنٌ (he is an ear), when he listens to what is said to him and accepts it.
[So the meaning is: if the matter is as they say, that he is close] to you, accepting your excuses.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿قُلْ أُذُنُ خَيْرٍ لَّكُمْ﴾.
That is, if he is as you have said.
Then He reported that he believes in Allah.
And whoever reads ﴿قل أُذْنٌ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ﴾ holds that its meaning is: Say: he is a listener [who is] good for you.

nahhas-meani:62-62.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَن يُرْضُوهُ﴾.
The meaning according to Sībawayh is: And Allah is more deserving that they should please Him, and His Messenger is more deserving that they should please him; then [one of the two] was elided, as the poet said:
نَحْنُ بِمَا عِنْدَنَا وَأَنْتَ بِمَا * عِنْدَكَ رَاضٍ، وَالرَّأْيُ مُخْتَلِفُ
(We are content with what we have, and you with what you have — and opinion differs.)
And Abū l-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad] said: It involves no elision, and the meaning is: And Allah is more deserving that they should please Him, and His Messenger.
And someone other than these two said: The meaning is: and the Messenger of Allah is more deserving that they should please him, and His saying, Mighty and Glorious, ﴿وَٱللَّهُ﴾ is an opening of speech, as you say: This is for Allah and for you.
